title: Post-deal rescue & recapture pocket — draft
summary: Pocket playbook for sellers and SEs to triage, re-engage, and recapture deals lost or cooled due to inference scale/latency/cost objections. Focuses on a lightweight technical triage, proposed quick POC options (hosted -> dedicated -> private), 90s messaging and email templates.
content:
OVERVIEW:
This is a compact, operational playbook for resurrecting deals that stalled or were lost because of inference economics, latency, or reliability concerns. Use when an opportunity has signaled: ‘too slow / too expensive / too risky to run at scale’.

Goal:
- Recapture a stalled deal within 2–4 weeks by offering a focused technical POC and a concrete remediation path.
- Move buyer from ‘no’ to ‘pilot’ by reducing perceived risk (tech, compliance, cost) and showing measurable unit economics improvements.

When to use (quick qualification):
- Deal lost in last 120 days, buyer cites performance, cost, or deployment risk.
- Contact still responsive on email or accepted an intro call.
- We can offer a 2–3 week tech POC with data-forward metrics.

90s Seller + SE pitch (script):
- Seller opener (30s): “We heard you on the concerns around latency and cost. We’ve run a rapid ‘rescue’ play with other infra teams — small POC surface, two-week window, measurable SLA and cost delta. No heavy lift.”
- SE follow (60s): “Technically, we’ll start by running a micro-profile of your typical request mix (2–4k requests) to reproduce latency/distribution. Then we’ll propose either (A) routing + batching config on hosted, (B) reserved Dedicated pool with predictable throughput, or (C) a VPC/private pilot if you need data residency. Each option has an expected latency/cost delta we’ll show in week 1.”

Triage checklist (first 48 hours):
- Get sample trafic and 10–50 representative requests (anonymized).
- Ask for top 3 SLOs: p50/p95 latency targets, cost per 1k tokens, availability SLA.
- Confirm constraints: data residency, encryption, network connectivity, egress.
- Determine current model & prompt shapes (seq len, few-shot examples).
- Run quick local profiling using our lightweight capture kit (SE script link: GH-PR-998) and return a 1-page heatmap.

Technical recapture playbook (3 paths):
- Path A — Fast hosted tuning (1 week):
  * Where to use: when buyer prefers no infra changes and wants price/latency tuning.
  * Actions: enable prefix/KV caching, reduce max tokens for streaming, enable continuous batching and set conservative batch_time_ms. Adjust model variant to a lower-cost quantized build for non-critical routes.
  * Deliverable: before/after p95 latency and per-1000-token cost estimate.

- Path B — Dedicated pilot (2 weeks):
  * Where to use: when buyer needs predictable throughput and isolation but not VPC.
  * Actions: map expected request qps to instance pool, provision reserved capacity for pilot (burst buffer enabled), run controlled load test with buyer traffic replay.
  * Deliverable: steady-state p95 under target qps, cost per hour and per-1M tokens, simple rollback plan.

- Path C — Private / VPC trial (3 weeks):
  * Where to use: compliance, data residency, or long-term TCO concerns.
  * Actions: small private control plane wiring, KMS integration mock, and a single on-prem/Dedicated endpoint. Focus scope: 1 service, 1 model variant, 2 SLOs.
  * Deliverable: validated end-to-end network flow, audit log snippet, and cost estimate for committed capacity.

Quick ROI sketch (one-pager):
- Inputs (ask buyer): monthly avg requests, avg tokens/request, target reduction in latency (%) and cost (%) required to continue.
- Output (deliverable): projection of token-cost savings over 12 months under Path B vs hosted baseline; break-even of reserved commit in months.
- Template: (we’ll fill with buyer numbers) e.g., 500k req/mo, 250 tokens/req -> 125M tokens/mo. If we can reduce per-1M token cost by $5 via batching/dedup/quantized model -> $625/mo saved; reserved commit effect shown separately.

Fast POC success metrics (what we promise in POC):
- Week 0–1: repeatable profiling and a recommended config.
- Week 1–2: measurable delta in p95 latency and cost-per-token for the chosen path.
- Acceptance criteria: 1 of the buyer SLOs met and an executive summary showing predicted 6–12 month TCO.

SE Play scripts (copy-ready)
- Email subject: Quick rescue POC — 2 week technical path to address latency/cost
- Email body (short):
  Hi <Name>,

  Thanks again for the honest feedback on <product/feature>. We ran a compact ‘rescue’ approach with similar customers and can offer a 2-week technical POC to directly address the latency and cost signals you saw.

  Plan: 1) We run a 48h traffic capture + profile, 2) propose 1 recommended config (hosted/Dedicated/VPC), 3) run a 1-week focused test and share results. No long-term commitment required.

  Can we schedule 30–45 minutes this week to align on the sample data and SLOs?

  — <Seller name> + <SE name>

- Call scoping bullets:
  * Confirm sample traffic and anonymization.
  * Confirm top 3 SLOs.
  * Agree POC guardrails and data to collect.

Escalation & internal steps (fast lane):
- If buyer is > $250k ARR potential: tag as high-priority and raise to AE + Solutions Eng lead.
- Technical blockers (KMS/network) -> loop in infra-sre and private-deployments PM with a 72h turn expectation.
- Exec ask (CISO/infra owner) -> book 1-hr stakeholder briefing with product security (Priya) and a short architecture diagram.

Mini-deck layout (use for quick 6-slide re-engage):
- Slide 1: Problem recap (buyer words) + impact statement.
- Slide 2: What we’ll prove in 2 weeks (SLO + acceptance criteria).
- Slide 3: Three recommended technical paths (A/B/C) with expected deltas.
- Slide 4: Quick ROI snapshot (fill with buyer numbers).
- Slide 5: POC timeline and low-friction onboarding checklist.
- Slide 6: Ask & next steps (decision point + meeting slots).

Common buyer objections + rebuttals (cheatcard):
- “We can’t risk downtime for experiments.” -> Offer read-only replay traffic, timeboxed test windows, and canary configuration on a shadow endpoint first.
- “Cost too high for hosted at scale.” -> Show batching and caching delta then present reserved Dedicated pricing. Use concrete token math.
- “Security/compliance concerns.” -> Offer VPC/private pilot, KMS proof-of-ownership flow, and point to audit log snippet from prior pilot.

Notes-to-self / open questions: 
- Need a trimmed demo capture kit (two scripts) for fast profiling; SEs find GH-PR-998 too heavy. Create lightweight zip by end of Q1.
- Create a simple spreadsheet template for ROI calc pre-filled with conservative estimates.
- Get a pre-approved 2-week pilot contract template from legal to remove procurement friction.

Next steps (internal):
1) Share this doc with AE and SE teams and run one mock rescue this month.
2) Align with product on three canonical pilot configs and publish them as canned options in Console.
3) Track results in JIRA-RECOVERY sprint board and measure recapture win rate after 3 months.

Appendix (useful quick links):
- Profiling kit (internal GH): GH-PR-998
- Prior pilot executive summary (anonymized): confluence://post-deal-recapture-playbook
- Sample pilot contract template: JIRA-INC-4321

Internal notes: informal, use for seller training, do not share externally without legal sign-off.

End of draft.
